no_assumption_attrition_bounds.scale: binary outcome difference, treatment offer minus control
no_assumption_attrition_bounds.assumptions: outcome lies in [0,1]; no assumption about outcomes for wave-3 nonrespondents
no_assumption_attrition_bounds.scope: finite public-use application-file cohort; omits sampling uncertainty and the published mixed-arm partnership exclusion/weighting, so it is not a no-interference ITT bound

assignment_to_interview_lag.interpretation: assignment-to-interview measurement lag; label-release time is not recorded

data_handling.report_contains: aggregate counts, schema names/labels, missingness, and linkage counts only
data_handling.missingness_semantics: pandas system-missing values only; codebook-coded skip, dont-know, and refusal values remain numeric and require field-specific recoding

limitations: The final report explains the 4,198-to-4,197 difference as removal of one nonrandomly assigned applicant; its 120 mixed-arm business-partnership exclusions cannot be recreated from the public-use application schema because partnership identifiers are absent.
This is fixed-horizon intention-to-treat evidence, not an event-level stream or delayed-feedback evaluation.
Wave response is differential by treatment arm; population policy values require explicit missingness assumptions and sensitivity analysis.
Aggregate missing-cell counts do not classify codebook-coded skip, dont-know, or refusal values as missing outcomes.
DOL reports an invoice-based program-group cost of $1,321 per member, but the extracted summary does not identify its dollar year or a cost suitable for individualized policy evaluation.
This dataset is a development candidate until a final split and outcome contract are frozen; no policy evaluation has been run.
